claims.content: Customer
The use case is triggered when the Customer clicks the 'Create New Auctions' button in the Auction Administration workspace.
An auction event is created containing all selected items with their applied and/or manually input data parameters.
The opening time for the auction group has been system-generated (calculated) once the duration and ending time are filled in.
After the use case completes successfully, the system displays the Auction Administration workspace with the 'View / Edit Current or Scheduled Auctions' interface populated with search results.
The Customer is a registered user.
The Customer has Administrator-level access or has been granted the specific permission 'Permission to create new auctions' via Yes/No radio buttons.
The Auction Admin Main Menu page is open in the web-based Auction Administration workspace.
The Customer’s objective is to list personal jewelry items for auction on the JTVauctions platform by creating a new auction event containing selected personal jewelry items.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer’s objective is to list personal jewelry items for auction on the JTVauctions platform by creating a new auction event containing selected personal jewelry items.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Using the auction-creation/listing workflow, the Customer selects one or more personal jewelry item(s), applies or manually inputs their data parameters, and the system creates a new auction event/listing containing the selected personal jewelry item(s).
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer initiates the auction-creation/listing workflow for personal jewelry items.
scope_contract.success_boundary: A new auction event/listing has been created containing the selected personal jewelry item(s) with their applied/manually input data parameters.
in_scope_actions: Selecting personal jewelry item(s) for auction
Applying and/or manually inputting data parameters for the selected personal jewelry item(s)
Creating the new auction event/listing containing the selected personal jewelry item(s)
excluded_adjacent_actions: User permission or Administrator role configuration
Opening/accessing the Auction Admin Main Menu as a separate administrative task
Creating or editing reusable auction event profile templates (cost tiers, opening bids, bid increments, durations)
Bidding, checkout, payment, or post-auction settlement
variant_dimensions: Number of personal jewelry item(s) selected
Selectable auction event type/profile if offered by the listing workflow

missing_aspects: Explicit evidence supporting that the customer 'manually inputs data parameters' (as opposed to applying existing ones) is not found in the cited cards. EC-G-010 mentions 'applied and/or manually input', but the source page (Table of Contents) does not explicitly describe the manual input action.

claims.content: If the Auctioneer attempts to apply a profile configured for 'Apply to Gemstones Only' to a grouping of jewelry items, the system generates an error message stating that this profile can only be applied to products in the gemstone category (retail category = gemstones).

The scheduling application prevents the creation of an auction with the same starting and ending date/time. This results in an error message, and the system highlights (color-codes) the offending data.

Before the auction is created, if any of the items being scheduled have additional quantities of the same item already scheduled in overlapping auction events, the system provides a warning, preferably via a popup window.

missing_aspects: Recovery/continuation after the profile-category mismatch error is not documented.
Recovery/continuation after the same start/end validation error is not documented.
Whether auction creation may proceed after the overlapping-quantity warning, or must be resolved first, is not documented.
Evidence does not support mapping this event to 'main-flow step 3', nor does it mention a 'Customer' (source uses 'Auctioneer').
Evidence does not support mapping this event to 'main-flow step 4', nor does it mention a 'Customer' (source uses 'Auctioneer').

claims.content: After clicking the 'Create New Auctions' button in the Auction Administration interface, the workflow is initiated by selecting search parameters (e.g., 'Scheduled Auctions', 'Current Auctions', or 'Both'), entering criteria (e.g., Product ID, Schedule Date, or Cost Range), and clicking the 'Find Product' button to locate items.

The system displays the matching jewelry items in the Search Results Section with Action checkboxes and item/auction information such as Product ID, Description, Unit Cost, Duration, Starts/Ends, and Increment.
The Customer selects one or more personal jewelry items from the search results list by checking the checkboxes in the Action column.

The Customer applies and/or manually inputs the auction data parameters for the selected items, including reserve amounts, bid increments, duration, and start/end times, using the available edit fields, Action dropdown bulk actions, a predefined auction profile, or manual reserve/cost fields.
The Customer clicks the 'Create New Auction' button, located at the bottom right of the interface.
The system creates the auction event containing the selected personal jewelry items with their applied and/or manually input data parameters.

Diverges from Step 3: Instead of manually selecting specific items, the Auctioneer uses the Auto-Scheduler capability to randomly choose products and schedule them over a chosen timeframe using given parameters.
Diverges from Step 3: The Auctioneer turns on the autofilter checkbox above the search results to filter the results, then selects one or more items from the filtered list.

Diverges from Step 4: Instead of setting starting/ending times via the available edit fields or Action dropdown bulk actions, the Customer applies the starting/ending time to all selected items by choosing the time from the dropdown list in the column header.

missing_aspects: The claim refers to 'personal jewelry items' which is not explicitly supported by the evidence text (which only mentions 'products').
The claim refers to 'Action checkboxes' which are not mentioned in the cited evidence.
The claim refers to 'personal jewelry items' which is not explicitly supported by the evidence text (which only mentions 'search results').
The claim implies selection follows filtering, but the evidence only describes the existence of the filter capability.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger is the Customer clicking 'Create New Auctions' in the Auction Administration workspace. Main Flow step 1 instead says 'The Auctioneer initiates the workflow by selecting search parameters ... and clicking Find Product.' This changes the primary actor and replaces the triggering action with a different search-initiation action, so the Main Flow does not continue from the Trigger. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (No cited evidence supports the Customer, rather than the Auctioneer, selecting the search parameters and clicking 'Find Product'.))

[goal_mainflow_alignment] Main_flow step 1 assigns the initiating action to 'the Auctioneer', but the goal scope contract states that the Customer initiates the auction-listing workflow. This makes the main flow's trigger step inconsistent with the goal's start boundary. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (No cited evidence supports the Customer, rather than the Auctioneer, selecting the search parameters and clicking 'Find Product'.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] The overlapping-quantity warning branch ends with 'the system provides a warning' but does not state whether auction creation is prevented, proceeds despite the warning, or returns to a main-flow step. The branch therefore lacks a clear terminal/prevention outcome. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 ends with the system providing a warning popup about overlapping quantities, but does not state whether auction creation is blocked, may proceed after acknowledgement, or is aborted. This is not a clear terminal failure/prevention state or return/hand-off. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Main Flow step 4 allows the Customer to manually input start/end times as part of the auction data parameters, but Postcondition 2 asserts that the opening time is system-generated/calculated from duration and ending time. A manually supplied start/end time would conflict with a system-calculated opening time, so the Main Flow does not consistently lead to this Postcondition.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception-flow claim 3 ends with 'the system provides a warning, preferably via a popup window' but does not state whether auction creation is blocked, whether the user must resolve the overlap before continuing, or whether the warning can be dismissed and the main flow resumes. This leaves the branch without a clear terminal/prevention state or return path.

inconsistency_hints: Postcondition 3 requires the Auction Administration workspace to display the 'View / Edit Current or Scheduled Auctions' interface with search results, but the Main Flow ends at step 6 with the system creating the auction event. No Main Flow step narrates the display/navigation to that interface, so the Postcondition is not reached by the described flow.

Main Flow step 1 uses a different actor ('Auctioneer') and a different initiation action ('selecting search parameters... clicking Find Product') than the Trigger ('Customer clicks Create New Auctions'). This is a discontinuity/restart rather than a compatible continuation from the Trigger.

Main flow claim 0 has the Auctioneer initiate the workflow via search, while the goal slot's start boundary says the Customer initiates the auction-creation/listing workflow. The Customer appears later, but the initiating actor/goal alignment is broken.

Postcondition 3 asserts a state reached after clicking 'Apply Changes' and displaying the 'View / Edit Current or Scheduled Auctions' interface, but the Main Flow never performs an 'Apply Changes' action. The flow instead goes from parameter entry/application to clicking 'Create New Auction' and system creation, so this postcondition is not reachable from the flow as written.
